title: When it gets hard, do not turn your back.
subtitle: Staying with your people at the hardest moment
then: Ibn Kathir explains the verse as a warning against {trap}running from the battle and leaving fellow Muslims behind.{/trap} Ibn Umar and Umar both said it was first about the day of Badr. The point was loyalty: {idea}when the line holds together, each person holds a place.{/idea}
now: The group project falls apart and you go quiet in the chat. The family crisis hits and you suddenly have too much work. The team takes the blame and you let it. {idea}Your place in the line matters, especially when it is hard.{/idea}
old: When things get rough, I can quietly step back and protect myself.
new: When I step back at the hard moment, someone else carries my share.
try: Think of one person facing something hard alone. Show up for them today, even in a small way.

title: Stepping back to regroup is not running away.
subtitle: The difference between strategy and desertion
then: The verse makes room for two reasons to pull back: {idea}as a tactic, or to join another group of one's own.{/idea} Umar said, {reward}we are the troop of every Muslim.{/reward} Fleeing for any other reason was counted among the great sins, and the verse warns of Allah's anger for it.
now: Taking a week off to recover so you can keep caring for your mother is not giving up. Asking a colleague for help is not failure. {trap}Disappearing so no one can reach you is different.{/trap} Be honest with yourself about which one you are doing.
old: Any time I step back, I am letting people down.
new: Stepping back to come back stronger is wise. Vanishing on people is not.
try: If you are stretched thin, ask one person for help today instead of quietly withdrawing.

title: You threw, but it was Allah who threw.
subtitle: The hand moves, the result is His
then: On the day of Badr the Prophet ﷺ prayed humbly in his shelter, then {idea}threw a handful of sand toward the enemy.{/idea} Allah made it reach their eyes. Ibn Kathir explains that the believers were few and the others many, so {reward}the victory was not from their own power.{/reward} The trial was a favor, so they would know it and be grateful.
now: You closed the deal. The surgery went well. Your child turned out kind. It is easy to take the bow. {idea}You did your part, and Allah made it land.{/idea} Gratitude keeps success from going to your head.
old: I worked hard, so the result is mine.
new: I did the throwing. Allah made it reach. The thanks go to Him.
try: Think of your latest success. Say alhamdulillah out loud and name what Allah did in it.

title: Allah weakens the schemes against the truth.
subtitle: More good news after the victory
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}more good news, on top of the victory.{/reward} Allah told the believers that the schemes of those who fought them would be {idea}weakened and brought to nothing.{/idea} The few at Badr did not need to out-plot anyone.
now: The coworker angling for your position. The rumor someone started about you. The person who seems to always be one move ahead. {idea}You do not need to scheme back.{/idea} Stay honest, do your work, and trust that crooked plans have a way of falling apart.
old: If someone is plotting against me, I have to out-plot them.
new: I don't need to scheme. Allah weakens plots, and honesty is my part.
try: If you are tempted to get back at someone, choose not to today. Ask Allah to handle it.

title: You asked for a verdict. The verdict came.
subtitle: A prayer that judged the one who prayed it

row.title: that cut family ties
sub: sure it was the other side

then: Abu Jahl prayed on the day of Badr: {trap}O Allah, whichever side cut family ties and brought what we do not know, destroy him today.{/trap} The verse answers: the verdict you asked for has come. Then it leaves a door open: {idea}if you stop, it is better for you.{/idea}
now: In a family fight you say, let Allah be the judge between us, certain the verdict will be yours. You pray for the other side to be exposed. {idea}Before asking for a ruling, ask whether you are the one in the wrong.{/idea}
old: I am so sure I'm right that I'll let Allah decide.
new: Before I ask Allah to judge between us, I should look honestly at myself.
try: In one disagreement you are in, write down one thing the other person might be right about.

title: Do not turn away while you are hearing.
subtitle: Knowing, then walking off anyway
then: After the battle scenes, the verse speaks to the believers directly. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}obey Allah and His Messenger ﷺ,{/idea} and do not turn from him {trap}after you have come to know his message.{/trap} The words in the verse are while you hear.
now: The Friday sermon lands right on your situation. You nod. By the time you reach the car, you are already on your phone and it is gone. {trap}Hearing and then turning away is its own choice.{/trap}
old: I listen to reminders. That is already something.
new: Hearing is the start. Turning away after I heard is what the verse warns against.
try: Recall the last reminder that hit home. Act on one small piece of it today.

title: Saying we heard, while not really hearing.
subtitle: The gap between nodding and listening
then: Ibn Ishaq said this refers to {trap}the hypocrites, who pretend to hear and obey while doing neither.{/trap} The believers are told not to become like them. Hearing, in this verse, means {idea}hearing that leads to doing.{/idea}
now: Your spouse asks you to stop doing that one thing. You say, I hear you. Next week, same thing. Your kid talks while you scroll and you say, mm-hm. {idea}Real hearing shows up the next day.{/idea}
old: I heard it, I agreed with it, so I listened.
new: I only truly heard it if it changes what I do.
try: Next time someone close to you speaks, put the phone face down and repeat back what they said.

title: Deaf and dumb by choice, refusing to think.
subtitle: Having ears and reason, and not using them

picture.label: What they have and don't use

then: Ibn Kathir explains these are people {trap}who do not hear the truth and do not grasp it.{/trap} Every creature follows the way it was made for, but these were made to worship Allah and refused. It is not about physical ability. It is about {idea}a mind and heart switched off by choice.{/idea}
now: There are topics where you have stopped listening. Any reminder about that habit, and you change the subject or roll your eyes. {idea}That is the small, private version of what this verse describes.{/idea} You still have time to open the door.
old: I am not like those people. I'm open-minded.
new: Everyone has a topic they refuse to hear. I should find mine.
try: Pick one reminder you usually tune out. Listen to it fully once today, without arguing back.

title: Had there been good in them, they would have heard.
subtitle: Hearing is a gift that follows a good heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains that if Allah had seen any good in them, {idea}He would have helped them understand.{/idea} Even if they had understood, {trap}they would have turned away out of stubbornness.{/trap} The problem was not missing information. It was missing intention.
now: You keep saying you'll pray more once you understand it better, read one more book, watch one more lecture. Sometimes understanding is not the gap. {idea}Wanting the good is.{/idea} Ask for that first.
old: If I just had more knowledge, I'd change.
new: Understanding comes to the heart that sincerely wants the good.
try: Make a short dua today: O Allah, put the wish for good in my heart.

title: Answer the call that gives you life.
subtitle: And know that hearts can turn

row.title: Allah
sub: between a man and his heart

row.title: later
sub: my heart will still be willing

then: Abu Sa'id bin Al-Mu'alla was praying when the Prophet ﷺ called him, and he finished first. The Prophet ﷺ cited this verse and then {reward}taught him the greatest surah, Al-Fatihah.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ often prayed: {idea}O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion.{/idea}
now: You feel moved to start praying again, to call your estranged brother, to quit the thing. The feeling is warm right now. {idea}Answer it today.{/idea} The heart that wants it now is a gift, and hearts can change.
old: I'll respond when I feel more ready.
new: The readiness I feel now is a gift. Hearts turn, so I should answer while it's here.
try: Say the dua: O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion. Then act on one good urge.

title: Some trials do not stop at the wrongdoers.
subtitle: When silence lets harm spread to everyone
then: Ibn Abbas said Allah told the believers {idea}to stop wrong from spreading among them{/idea} so the trial would not cover everyone. The Prophet ﷺ gave the parable of a ship: people below wanted to drill a hole for water. {trap}If the others let them, all would drown.{/trap} If they held their hands, all would be saved.
now: The cousin everyone knows is in trouble but no one wants to bring it up. The office habit of fudging numbers that nobody questions. The group chat joke that keeps getting meaner. {idea}You are on the same boat.{/idea} A kind, honest word can save more than one person.
old: As long as I'm not doing wrong, it's not my problem.
new: We share the boat. Gently holding back a wrong protects everyone, including me.
try: Is there one harmful thing around you that everyone ignores? Raise it gently with one person today.

title: Remember when you were few and afraid.
subtitle: Looking back to see how far He brought you
then: In Makkah the believers were {trap}few, practicing in secret, afraid of being snatched away.{/trap} Allah gave them a safe home in Madinah, with the people there sheltering and supporting them. Qatadah said: {reward}your Lord gives favors and loves to be praised, and those who thank Him are given more.{/reward}
now: The first tiny apartment. The year you could not pay the bills. The months you had no one. Now you have a steady job, a home, people. {idea}It is easy to forget the beginning.{/idea} Remembering it is how gratitude stays alive.
old: That hard time is behind me. Better not to think about it.
new: Remembering where I started shows me how much Allah has given me.
try: Write down three things you have now that you didn't have five years ago. Thank Allah for each.

title: Do not betray what you were trusted with.
subtitle: Every duty is a trust you carry
then: Ibn Kathir mentions Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah, who wrote to Quraysh warning them of a coming march. The Prophet ﷺ spared him because he had been at Badr. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}the verse is general{/idea} and betrayal includes {trap}minor and major sins and those that harm others.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said the trust is the duties Allah gave you.
now: The friend's secret you shared just once. The work laptop used for side business. The hours billed but not worked. The prayer you were trusted with and pushed aside. {idea}Each one is a trust.{/idea}
old: Betrayal is something dramatic. I'm not that kind of person.
new: Small trusts count too: secrets, time, money, and my duties to Allah.
try: Pick one trust you've been careless with lately, and make it right today.

title: Your wealth and children are a test.
subtitle: Gifts that can pull you closer or away
then: This verse follows the warning about betraying trusts. Ibn Kathir explains that Allah gives wealth and children {idea}to see who stays grateful and obedient, and who becomes absorbed in them instead of Him.{/idea} {reward}With Allah is a greater reward.{/reward}
now: Late at the office again, for the kids, you tell yourself. Skipping prayer because the baby needed you. A small lie at work to protect the bonus. {idea}Loving them is good. Letting them pull you from Allah is the test.{/idea}
old: Everything I do for my family is automatically good.
new: My family and money are a gift and a test. The question is whether they bring me closer.
try: Do one thing with your children today that also reminds you of Allah, like a short dua together.
